creative.title: The Art
paragraphs: Away from programming I draw and I care about the small details, which might explain my relationship with the frontend because even though my work revolves around the backend I still like having a share of the side we actually see
Making something work the way it should is just as satisfying to me as making it look the way I imagined

teaching.title: An Attempt at Explaining
paragraphs: At one point I decided to share what I knew with university students, with more enthusiasm than resources, a microphone that wasn't at its best and a voice that sometimes sounded like it was fighting sleep (and the sleepiness was real by the way, just a university student doing her best)
Whenever I go back to those recordings some of the details make me cringe a little, but I still love the genuine wish to share what I knew even if the result wasn't perfect

I stopped recording but I never stopped loving to explain
I still enjoy simplifying ideas and sharing what I learn with others, and explaining something often helps me understand it more deeply
teaching.warning: Gentle warning: you may catch a yawn between explanations

experience.title: Professional Experience
experience.intro: My experience in software development goes beyond writing code. It starts with understanding and analyzing requirements and translating them into software solutions, and extends to developing systems, reviewing code and investigating and resolving production issues. I enjoy challenges that require research, analysis and attention to detail, especially when they lead me to discover better ways to solve problems or improve existing systems.
experience.areas_note: A selection of functional areas and systems I contributed to through development, review and improvement work in a real production environment.

arch_text: I've worked on backend services using a Microservices architecture and also gained experience with a different architectural approach using a Monolith.

This experience helped me better understand the practical differences between both architectures and the challenges each one brings, including when separating services makes sense and when a simpler approach might be more suitable.

troubleshooting.title: When Things Go Wrong in Production
troubleshooting.intro: My work doesn't end when a feature is delivered. I also investigate production issues by tracing errors, analyzing logs, monitoring application performance and identifying root causes. I enjoy this side of engineering because it reveals how systems actually behave beyond what we expect.
troubleshooting.flow_note: Not a fixed sequence. Each incident can start in a different place with a different tool.
